classification.difficultyReason: Part (a) requires recognising that the equality marks establish only a square base, not a cube, and concluding that the unlabelled height prevents a numerical surface area. This assessment of insufficient information is the hardest demand; part (b) directly applies the taught face-pair method.

content.prompt: Find the surface area of the following prisms.

spec.description: Rectangular prism with two single equality ticks on the front lower edge and lower right receding edge. No height label or height equality tick is supplied. Ordinary source blue and red strokes become black; hidden edges remain dashed.
spec.mathematics: Two adjacent base edges are equal and measure 8.2 m. The height is unspecified.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and equality marks are visible.

answer.short: Insufficient information: the height is missing.
answer.worked:
The equality marks give a square base of side $8.2\,\mathrm{m}$, but do not establish the height. If the height is $h$ metres, the face-pair method gives
$$\begin{aligned}A&=2(8.2\times8.2)+2(8.2h)+2(8.2h)\\A&=134.48+32.8h\quad\mathrm{m}^2.\end{aligned}$$
A numerical surface area requires the height. If the intended solid is a cube, its surface area is $403.44\,\mathrm{m}^2$.

spec.description: Tall rectangular prism with depth receding towards the upper left, labelled 1 cm, 2 cm and 3 cm. Source decorative edge colours are replaced by black, retaining hidden-edge dashes.
spec.mathematics: Rectangular prism dimensions 1 cm by 2 cm by 3 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: Dimensions only; no answer appears in the question diagram.

answer.worked:
Front and back: $(1\times3)\times2=6\,\mathrm{cm}^2$.

Sides: $(2\times3)\times2=12\,\mathrm{cm}^2$.

Top and bottom: $(1\times2)\times2=4\,\mathrm{cm}^2$.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=6+12+4\\A&=22\,\mathrm{cm}^2.\end{aligned}$$
